title: Filtering Numbers in JavaScript
summary: By the end, you'll understand how to filter numbers in an array using JavaScript.

scenes.narration: Welcome to our lesson on filtering numbers in JavaScript. By the end, you'll know how to pick specific numbers from an array.
scenes.heading: Filtering Numbers in JavaScript
scenes.subheading: Learn how to filter numbers in an array using JavaScript.

scenes.narration: First, we create an array called 'nums' with some numbers inside. Think of it like a box of different-sized toys.
Next, we use the 'filter' method on 'nums'. It's like sifting through the box to find only the bigger toys.
Here's our 'nums' array before we filter it. We have the numbers three, eight, one, ten, and six.
After filtering, we keep only the numbers greater than five. So, we end up with eight, ten, and six.
Finally, we print the filtered array using 'console.log'. This shows us the result in the console.
And here's the output: an array containing the numbers eight, ten, and six. These are the numbers greater than five from our original array.
To sum up, we created an array of numbers, filtered out the ones greater than five, and printed the result. Now you can do the same with any array of numbers!
points: We created an array called 'nums' with some numbers.
We used the 'filter' method to keep only the numbers greater than five.
We printed the filtered array to see the result.
